known.title: The machine-path lookbehind does not accept a single quote, so a home or temporary path in single quotes gets no advice.
known.summary: MACHINE_PATH (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/scripts/plan.mjs:29) starts a match only at a line start, after white space, after file://, or after one of the marks ( " ` [ { = : ; , >. The single quote is not in this list. The old regex of the base commit had it, and the double quote and the backtick are still in the list. Thus a machine path that opens with a single quote gets no advice: "cd '/home/<user>/clone'" and the node:assert output "'/tmp/run-1/out.json' !== 'x'" give no advice line, but the same paths in double quotes or backticks do. Shell commands quote paths this way (POSIX 2.2.2: 'Enclosing characters in single-quotes ('') shall preserve the literal value of each character within the single-quotes.', https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9799919799/utilities/V3_chap02.html#tag_19_02_02), and node:assert prints strings in single quotes (https://nodejs.org/api/assert.html#assertstrictequalactual-expected-message, example output "+ 'Hello foobar'"). plan-contract.md:218-222 defines a machine path by its root and has no exception for quoted text. Plan decision 1 (plan line 26) flags every machine root. No row of scripts/tests/plan-cli.mjs:262-287 has a path in single quotes, so the suite passes.

known.title: The machine-path scan reads the raw input instead of the normalized body that plan.mjs writes, so a path next to an em dash gets no advice or a wrong name.
known.summary: normalizePlan makes `cleaned` (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/scripts/plan.mjs:525-529): it changes CRLF to LF and each U+2014 em dash to ' - '. It writes the body from `cleaned` (plan.mjs:530 and 572), and plan-contract.md:206-208 says that writes change U+2014 to ' - '. But the scan on plan.mjs:570 runs MACHINE_PATH on `text`, the raw input. The base commit scanned `cleaned`. U+2014 (Unicode category Pd) is not white space (MDN: '\s Matches any whitespace or line terminator character.', https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Regular_expressions/Character_class_escape), and it is not in the lookbehind or in the stop set of plan.mjs:29. Thus `edit` (plan.mjs:792) and `new` (plan.mjs:706) read another text than the body that plan.mjs writes. 'The scratch folder—/tmp/run-1—keeps the logs.' gives no advice, but the written body holds ' - /tmp/run-1 - ', and a later `show` (plan.mjs:731) advises. 'Logs stay in /tmp/run-1—the helper keeps them.' gives the advice '/tmp/run-1—the', a text that is not in the written body. No row of scripts/tests/plan-cli.mjs:262-287 has an em dash, so the suite passes.

known.title: The machine-path test only checks that each expected line is in the advice, so the negative rows assert nothing.
known.summary: scripts/tests/plan-cli.mjs:289 runs assert.ok(machinePathAdvice(text).includes(line)) once for each line of `expected`. The six negative rows (plan-cli.mjs:282-287: URL routes, TMPDIR=/tmp, /usr/bin paths, awk and PHP text, URLs, bare /tmp and /home/, escaped regex text) have an empty `expected`, so the loop body does not run and these rows check nothing. The positive rows also do not fail on an extra, repeated, or out-of-order advice line. The test comment (plan-cli.mjs:255-256) and plan-contract.md:221-223 promise one line per distinct path and no advice for URL routes and portable system paths, and plan decision 3 (plan line 28) requires body order. Checked with a copy of plan.mjs whose tmp branch matches a bare /tmp ((?:tmp|var\/tmp)\b): two rows fail the whole-value deepEqual of the base test, but no row fails the seeded check.

known.title: The character after a home or temporary root can be a backtick, a quote, or a parenthesis, so a bare root in a code span or in quotes gets advice.
known.summary: In MACHINE_PATH (plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/scripts/plan.mjs:29), a home or mount root (/home/, /Users/, /root/, /mnt/, ...) and a temporary root (/tmp/, /var/tmp/, /private/tmp/) must have one more character from the class [^\s/]. This character is the guard that keeps a bare root out of the advice: the comment at plan.mjs:26-27 says 'a bare /tmp do not match', plan-contract.md:222-223 says 'a bare `/tmp`, get no advice', and plan decision 1 (plan line 26) says the same. The class now accepts the backtick, both quotes, and ')', which close a code span, a quoted string, or a parenthesis (MDN: '[^abc] matches any character except a, b, or c', https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Regular_expressions/Character_class). Thus 'Write scratch files only under `/tmp/`.' gives the advice '/tmp/`', and '"/tmp/" or (/home/)' gives '/tmp/"' and '/home/)': false advice for a portable directory, with a closing mark in the name. The bare-root row (scripts/tests/plan-cli.mjs:286) has bare roots only before a space or a line end, so the suite passes.
